issues.detail: The Greek 'πορευθεις' (poreutheis) is a perfect passive participle, implying 'having gone' or 'having ascended'. The Vietnamese 'đã đi' (past tense) combined with 'hiện đang ở' (present continuous/state) captures the result but misses the specific nuance of the completed action of ascending that leads to the current state. More importantly, the Greek structure implies 'having ascended into heaven [where he is] on the right hand of God', whereas the Vietnamese phrasing slightly decouples the movement and the location.

The Greek 'υποταγεντων αυτω' (hypotagentōn autō) is a participle modifying the angels, powers, and mighty ones. The Vietnamese 'đều phục dưới Ngài' (all serve/are under Him) changes the grammatical relationship from a descriptive participle to a general statement of fact about their status.
